source.title: ACTR: Aligning Thoughts and Responses for Multilingual Safety in Reasoning LLMs
source.authors: Xian-Hui Zhang; Jian Yu; Cheng-Yu Xie; Chen-Hang Cui; Shu-Yi Miao; Pengyang Shao; Yu Zheng; Fei Shen; Tat-Seng Chua

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly assumes a linear safety direction in its theoretical justification, citing prior work, but does not test that direction. Its own mechanistic intervention identifies and masks safety think neurons instead.
record.gate_note: The paper does not find a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction, ablate or add such a direction, or test a weight edit. Table 3 reports ASR after masking a different object—identified safety think neurons—so those results are recorded as bearing on the subject but not on a listed claim version. Other ASR results concern the paper's training method or baselines, not a test of the claimed direction.
record.test_reason: The study never computes, ablates, adds or weight-edits a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. Its causal test masks its own 'safety think neurons', which are attention Q/K/V/O rows and columns chosen by think-on vs think-off importance. A linear 'safety direction' appears only as Assumption 1 in the Appendix B justification of TGS, citing Meng et al. and Zou et al. Arditi et al. is cited only in related work. So the study assumes, and does not test, the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find a think–response disconnect in non-high-resource languages: English think traces flag the risk, yet responses are unsafe. Masking safety think neurons raises ASR and TGS. Their method, ACTR/NSCO, trains only those neurons with a consistency reward, lowers ASR, generalizes to unseen languages, and preserves utility with low benign refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper identifies neurons by contrasting think-on and think-off importance, then masks or selectively trains their associated parameters. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless activation-difference direction or its residual-stream projection intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The neuron-selection threshold affects general capability: the paper reports sharp MGSM degradation above p = 3%. Its analysis also compares targeted neuron masking with count- and layer-matched random masking.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking about 3% of attention projection neurons, chosen as important when think mode is on but not when it is off, raises multilingual jailbreak ASR. Gemma4-12B-it rises 7.89→51.79 on MultiJail and 2.30→40.52 on AdvBench-X; Qwen3-8B rises 15.46→31.07 and 10.27→16.32. Count- and layer-matched random masking changes ASR by at most 1.54 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning LLMs, a sparse set of attention neurons that carry the think span into the response is causally needed for safe responses to multilingual jailbreaks.

record.problems: The reported masking results have no uncertainty estimates stated. The intervention targets a neuron set identified by the paper's own procedure, not the claimed single direction, and the paper's theoretical justification assumes a linear safety direction rather than testing it.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Other reported measurements concern attention-based think utilization, consistency rates, or outcomes of the paper's own training method; they do not measure or intervene on the claimed refusal direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is identified, ablated or added. There are no induce-refusal or capability tests of such a direction.
No abliteration or weight edit of a refusal direction.
No test of whether jailbreaks suppress the direction. No training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multi-direction structure.
No test separating the harmfulness representation from the refusal decision. The think-vs-response safety mismatch is behavioural, not representational.
Multilingual ASR is measured, but transfer of a refusal direction across languages or models is not tested.
The models are reasoning models, but no refusal direction is tested in them.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche from the record are kept. The Appendix B linear safety direction is a theoretical assumption that is never estimated, so it gives no evidence on V1. TN-masking rows r2, r4, r6 and r8 measure ASR on harmful prompts only, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is identified, ablated, or added; no benign-request refusal or general-capability effect of such an intervention is tested.
No ablation is converted into a weight edit, and no released-model abliteration is tested.
No attack is tested for suppressing the claimed direction, and no training against its ablation is tested.
The paper does not test whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
No separate encoding of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
Safety behavior is evaluated across languages and model variants, but transfer of the claimed direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
The paper trains its own method but does not test how training choices determine whether the claimed removable direction exists.
The models reason before answering, but the paper does not test the V1 direction or its ablation/addition in reasoning models.
